selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What central warning is given in this conclusion about worldly life?
questions.answer: Being absorbed in this life and forgetting the next life is a serious form of heedlessness and deception.

questions.question: What Qur’anic idea is brought at the beginning of the passage, and what does it say about worldly gain?
questions.answer: It teaches that the attractions of this world are misleading and should not be treated as lasting truth.

questions.question: How is the nafs described at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as spiritually careless, attached to worldly sweetness, forgetful of the hereafter, and focused only on this world.

questions.question: What animal is used in the comparison?
questions.answer: An ostrich.

questions.question: What does the ostrich do when it notices the hunter?
questions.answer: It hides its head in the sand because it cannot escape by flying.

questions.question: What mistake does the ostrich make in that image?
questions.answer: It acts as if not seeing the hunter means the hunter does not see it, while its body remains exposed.

questions.question: How does that inability shape its behavior?
questions.answer: Since it cannot flee, it chooses a false way of coping by hiding its head.

questions.question: What does the title-like note calling the passage “a slap for the heedless and a warning lesson” suggest about its tone?
questions.answer: The tone is meant to be sharp, corrective, and awakening rather than gentle or merely descriptive.

questions.question: What is the first spiritual problem named in the passage?
questions.answer: Heedlessness.

questions.question: What two attachments are linked together in the description of the nafs?
questions.answer: Love of worldly life and forgetfulness of the hereafter.

questions.question: How does the passage portray worldly life when it is loved in the wrong way?
questions.answer: It appears attractive, but that attraction misleads people.

questions.question: What does the verse at the opening contribute to the meaning of the passage?
questions.answer: It frames the whole warning by teaching that worldly possessions can deceive people about what truly matters.

questions.question: In the comparison, what inability does the ostrich have?
questions.answer: It cannot escape by flight.

questions.question: What does the exposed body of the ostrich imply in the comparison?
questions.answer: The person’s real condition is still open and vulnerable even if they try not to think about it.

questions.question: Why is the nafs called “wretched” in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it has fallen into a low state through carelessness, worldly attachment, and neglect of the hereafter.

questions.question: What does it mean here to say that the nafs sees life as sweet?
questions.answer: It is overly attracted to worldly pleasure and comfort.

questions.question: What has the nafs forgotten?
questions.answer: The hereafter.

questions.question: What does the nafs seek according to the passage?
questions.answer: It seeks only worldly life.

questions.question: What is the structure of the comparison used in the passage?
questions.answer: A spiritually heedless person is compared to an ostrich reacting foolishly to a hunter.

questions.question: What is irrational about the ostrich’s behavior?
questions.answer: It confuses its own lack of sight with actual safety.

questions.question: How does the hunter still have the advantage?
questions.answer: The hunter can still see the ostrich clearly because most of it remains uncovered.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage draw between heedlessness and the love of dunya?
questions.answer: It shows that heedlessness grows when a person becomes charmed by dunya and loses sight of the hereafter.

questions.question: Why is the worldly life called deceptive in the verse quoted here?
questions.answer: Because it can attract people with temporary pleasure and make them neglect what is permanent and true.

questions.question: In the example, what danger does the ostrich recognize?
questions.answer: It recognizes the hunter.
